FIRST FIRE · User manual · November 2026

From a claim to a source

Use this research desk to check what a space fire experiment actually measured, compare it with a mission environment, and decide what evidence you still need.

Open the AtlasDownload this guide as a PDFOpen the research deskTechnical manual

Your first three minutes

Suppose someone reports that a piece of Nomex fabric burned for 140 seconds on a spacecraft. The source has a 140-second entry. What was burning?

  1. Open Cases → Saffire-II. In Evidence, read the question about Nomex ignition. The experiment exposed two adjoining materials, PMMA (acrylic) and Nomex, to a flame.
  2. Open the data explorer for sample 2-7. Select the test number 2-7 to expand the original NASA row. The table lists “PMMA & Nomex” and a burn time of 140 s. That duration belongs to the assembly.
  3. Read Note 2 in the Original NASA table (local CSV), or open the investigator source on the case. The PMMA was consumed. The Nomex did not ignite in this test. Documented blackening alone cannot establish fabric ignition.
  4. Return to the case and open My research brief. Write which component ignited and one limit on applying this finding to a different atmosphere. Select Download brief to keep the finding and its citations together.
What changed? A true number supported the wrong claim when it was attached to only one component. Recording the sample, component and endpoint gives someone else a way to check your interpretation.

Opening the project

Unpack the complete download, open its dashboard index.html in a current browser, and keep the adjacent files together. Search, original CSV tables, habitat ranking and practice work offline. External NASA pages and ordinary web search need an internet connection. The Atlas covers 1,622 source records in 16 tables from 15 investigations. The Data explorer covers 1,058 individually normalized observations. The extended catalog includes 19 investigations. The four-view walkthrough is on page 7.

Worked example source · NASA PSI-99, v5, experimental table, sample 2-7 and Note 2.

Research workflow · Evidence and decisions

Find the right evidence

Start with a question

Use Find evidence on the Research desk for a subject such as “smoke from wire insulation.” Search ranks the published cases and investigation descriptions using a local semantic model and keyword matching. If model loading fails, the page identifies the keyword search. For an individual sample number, use Data explorer.

Follow a case

Read the Observed record. In Evidence comparison, choose a suggested question or select Ask your own question. In the SAME case, try “Did the detector miss Teflon smoke?” Read the matching evidence and open its source. If the case cannot support your question, the panel explains the gap. The Research decision below gives the authors’ interpretation and next test. Six design options compares their proposed approaches.

Open a caseThe distinction to look for
SIBALFlame spread speed versus time to visible extinction.
Saffire-IIDamage to a fabric versus ignition of that component.
FLEXLoss of visible flame versus the end of chemical heat release.
SAMEMeasured smoke particles versus reaching an alarm threshold.
CFI-GOxygen at the burner versus oxygen in the surrounding gas.
ICESA short partial-gravity observation versus an extrapolated limit.

Keep a usable brief

In My research brief, enter the decision, one limitation and the next measurement or reanalysis. Save on this device stores your answers in the current browser profile. Download brief exports plain text and the case's primary sources. Use the download for sharing or for a durable copy before clearing browser storage.

Check your own wording

Open Claim review, enter your question and choose Find relevant cases. Select the experiment you mean. Map your endpoint, material, gravity and intended assertion to the source. A mismatch or unknown condition produces an insufficient-support finding. Read the source locator and proposed next measurement, then save or download the review. Choose No applicable case to record a gap.

Sources & methods includes the Coverage map (choose a subject and counted field), Referee (test a quote, its interpretation and a supported number) and Project walkthrough. A matching quotation establishes where the words occur; you decide what they establish.

Data workflow · Observations and comparisons

Inspect a NASA record

In Data explorer → Observations, choose an investigation or subject. Search for a test ID, material or endpoint. Click a column heading to sort; click again to reverse it. Next and Previous move through the results. Click the test number to see the unmodified row and the fields FIRST FIRE interpreted.

Two oxygen fields can look identical

Choose CFI-G · PSI-159. Set minimum O₂ to 34 with the initial ambient oxygen field selected. You should find 113 observations. Switch the oxygen field to O₂ in burner stream. You should now see 106 different observations. An inverse burner feeds oxygen into a chamber containing fuel. An 85% burner stream does not describe an 85% habitat atmosphere. Choosing final oxygen asks another question again.

Trace or export

Export filtered CSV downloads every matching normalized record, across all pages. Original NASA table (local CSV) downloads the versioned archive table. The row locator counts the header as row 1. The DOI opens the investigation, and the versioned download identifies the upstream source file. The catalogue also links source tables that have no normalized observations.

Read the missing fields. An em dash or blank means the field is unavailable, inapplicable or excluded for a stated reason. A recorded zero is a value. Fan display, smoke inlet velocity and burner mass flow refer to different quantities. When an oxygen interval is given, the numeric filter includes records whose intervals overlap your selection.

Compare with a habitat

Open Rank for a habitat. Choose a scenario and required subject. Adjust gravity, ambient oxygen, absolute pressure and optional material text. Each investigation contributes its closest eligible record. Rows covering all three conditions rank ahead of rows with two or one, and the table names the missing fields. Inverse gas-burner oxygen is excluded from atmospheric comparisons.

Expand Weights and distance calculation to change which differences matter. The sensitivity panel doubles each weight separately and shows whether the leading investigation order changes. A close score still leaves questions about orientation, sample size, ventilation and the observed endpoint. The orbit rows use nominal zero g.

Comparison source · NASA PSI-159, v1, normal and inverse experimental tables.

Prediction workflow · Assumptions and scoring

Read the FM² forecast

Open FM² forecast to explore four planned fabric burns at 8.2 psia. The forecast asks whether flame keeps spreading after the igniter switches off. The fixed forecast has a signed timestamp dated 14 November 2026. The deposit package is available and a DOI is pending. Edit a separate scenario to explore possible outcomes. Official flight results are still pending.

Change the assumptions

Under Assumed oxygen limit, set the mean threshold and its spread in percentage points, or choose Set the central 80% interval directly and Use these bounds. The curve and the chances in Four planned burns update with your assumptions.

Read the fabric illustration

Select a starting oxygen level. At the default 25% O₂, the two views show the same vertical 2 × 20 cm Synergy Pro Navy strip under different assumed limits. Choose Play ignition to replay the bottom wire heating and switching off. With the default bounds, 25% exceeds the lower limit (24.08%), so the front advances upward in that view. It falls below the upper limit (27.92%), so the other view shows no sustained spread. Changing a burn or an assumption updates both views. The full distribution gives a 25.25% chance at 25% O₂. Flame speed and travel distance are illustrative.

Initial oxygen37%33%29%25%
Default chance of sustained spread>99.99%>99.99%97.72%25.25%

Choose a follow-up measurement

Choose the next oxygen test compares one test or a fixed pair. A yes/no result near a 50% prediction can narrow the estimated threshold. Igniter reliability, sample count and platform time also affect test choice.

Interpret a score

In Score hypothetical outcomes, mark each burn yes, no, pending or void. Both forecasts use the same resolved trials. Their Brier scores average the squared difference between each probability and observed outcome (1 or 0). Lower is better. The locked file specifies 90/90/90/10% for the project comparator. NASA supplied qualitative expectations. To score a future burn, verify the sample, atmosphere, igniter and outcome in a flight record. Keep interrupted or unreported trials out of the score.

Export this scenario downloads your edited inputs and displays their checksum. Compare them with the fixed forecast and its signed timestamp receipt. The fixed file also gives illustrative travel lengths of 20, 17.5, 7.5 and 0 cm at the mean limit.

Evaluation workflow · Hand-off and results

Run a blind comparison

Open Blind test. Practice with six published cases lets you learn the controls with known material. Practice files are excluded from study results. To measure a benefit, a facilitator supplies six previously unseen questions and keeps the independently authored assessor key private, with credit criteria agreed before use.

WhoWhat to do
FacilitatorAssign a unique anonymous slot from 1–12. Keep the assessor key private. Give participants equivalent source access, instructions and time limits. Supply only the participant pack. Across a run, each person uses FIRST FIRE for three cases and ordinary search for three.
ParticipantChoose the assigned slot and Import facilitator’s participant pack. Select Reveal prompt and start timer, then use the assigned method. Enter a decision, a primary citation and a limit. The optional budget question asks what to do next and why. Submit or let the deadline record the attempt.
AssessorLoad the assessor key and one masked response file. Score the decision, citation and scope separately. Score a budget choice only where the study defines its rubric. Export grades. Keep the analyst file with the facilitator so assignment and timing stay hidden.
AnalystImport the complete analyst records and the matching final grade files together. Review fully supported answers, correct sources, timeouts and median time. The optional budget measure has its own denominator. Export scores by case and participant.

Before leaving the device

The active participant run uses local browser storage. The deadline continues while you consult sources or leave the page. At the end select Export masked responses and Export analyst record. Export grades before leaving the assessor page. A partial record is available under Session controls after at least one completed response. Export before clearing the session or switching devices.

What is a real result? A completed facilitated run, matched to independently scored responses. This edition includes the protocol and practice materials. It has no published participant comparison. Report the number of people, missing sessions and uncertainty alongside any future result.

Study protocol · Rehearsal participant pack. Facilitators can find its example key in the full source project at research/evaluation-examples/key.example.json. Use a new private key for an authentic study.

Research chat

Ask, follow up, then check the source

Choose Chat in the top bar and enter your question. Open Explore for the case library, NASA records and benchmark.

Try a two-turn conversation

  1. Ask: “In Saffire-II sample 2-7, which material actually burned?” Open the cited flight report and check its sample number.
  2. Follow up: “Does the 140 seconds belong to the Nomex?” Check whether the answer separates the whole assembly from the fabric. If it does not, the linked source takes priority.
  3. Try a question the archive cannot settle: “What oxygen threshold is safe for my new spacesuit fabric?” A nearby material or a model probability cannot certify that fabric.

Read or revisit a reply

Select a numbered citation to open its source and check the measured conditions or the investigators’ findings. Choose Retry answer to try the same question in a separate chat. Refreshing the page opens an empty chat. Open History in the same browser tab to return to a previous conversation.

Start or reopen the local model

From the complete project, follow the setup steps in README and start the local server. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/#chat in your browser. A double-click on dist/index.html opens the archive edition instead. Set up model files once; an API key is not required for the local test.

Check an answer or change its reading level

For supported archive questions, open Check this answer to inspect its checks. In the Referee, select Test the planted quote and read the rejection reason. The public error log lists release examples. Your text stays on your device. In Reading preferences, pick an answer depth or use a local text, PDF or Word (.docx) résumé to suggest one. You can override that suggestion.

Inspect mistakes

In the benchmark, choose “Failed a check” and compare the reply with its source. The original local model passed 78/100. Applying today’s evidence checks to those saved answers gives 43/100. Both scored 14/24 on a separate set. A different test asks whether chat opened the right tool: the router scored 54/60 on new questions. Read the failures.

Team Code Blooded · Dashboard walkthrough

Follow a question across four views

The Gap · Which tests were actually flown?

Open Atlas. Select a gravity and starting-oxygen cell, then open a source row. A zero is the count for that selection. The diamond marks a planned FM² starting condition. Select SPICE in the investigation filter to see why its 469 burner settings cannot be counted as 469 separate burns. Download CSV includes all matching records and their source locators.

In Compass, choose a habitat and test subject. Check gravity, ambient oxygen and pressure for the closest test. In Atlas, open Compare two source records and select the chamber/burner pair. Only the chamber value describes the test atmosphere. Open each original row to see where NASA reported it.

The Audit · Does the claim transfer?

Rulebook checks seven questions across orbit, Moon and Mars, covering Earth screening, ventilation, specimen size, visible extinction, smoke detection, burn duration and burner oxygen. Select a rule and read its counterexample or unresolved condition. Open an investigation passport for the source version, scope and original CSV.

The Oracle · What would change the prediction?

Open the four-burn forecast and follow page 4. Use the what-if controls to score a hypothetical outcome and find the next oxygen level to test. Return to the signed forecast when comparing a future official result.

At Home · What else must be measured?

At Home relates the evidence to crew cabins, oxygen wards and confined spaces. For Gaganyaan, check both total pressure and oxygen fraction. For a hospital drape, ask about oxygen near the actual fabric and ignition source. Follow each source for the conditions of that example.

Test a cabin design

In Physics Lab, set a material, cabin volume, oxygen, pressure, spread speed and oxygen cutoff. Move the time control to read O₂, CO₂ and heat. In the rover sandbox, select or name a cabin, chassis and battery. Under Reverse the flow, select Compare both inputs. The Saffire-I rates give 10.8 and 7.8 cm after 60 seconds with the default cabin. These distances are model outputs.

Engine assumptions and verification · Try a source check in the Referee

Guided investigation

Run the four-step demonstration

Open Run the investigation on the home page, enter your question, and choose Start guided session. The thin navigation bar above each tool moves you forward or back to your research record.

1. Compare NASA experiments

In Matched experiments, keep the default methanol comparison and reveal the endpoints. The three burn durations change in different directions. Require the same test day and inspect how many pairs survive. A change in the average alone would miss this weakness.

2. Isolate a sensor

In Tracer transport, change from default exchange to isolated compartments. The source receives the same tracer, but the remote sensor never crosses its threshold. Increase circulation and scrub the timeline. Compare the fitted time with a Berkeley Lab repeat. Under Fit a sensor trace, load two local CSVs or try the synthetic pair. Train on the first run, then inspect the errors on the second.

3. Design a lunar follow-up

Start at 26% oxygen under the default assumptions. Record a hypothetical Spread sustained reading and inspect the next setting. Undo, record No sustained spread, and compare the other branch. Try optimizing the decision for a particular planned burn.

4. Ask the data and save your work

Ask “How many methanol observations are in FLEX?” Then ask for their mean burn duration. Inspect the reported and missing measurements and download the calculation receipt. Use Review session → Download research record to keep the question, current inputs, results and sources together.

Methods and limitations · Independent chat questions

Master edition

Build a cabin investigation

Choose the question and reading level

Open Your investigation. Check the suggested device tier and choose the example that fits your field. A résumé can suggest a level. Its contents are processed in your browser.

Compare the air and materials

Open Cabin air. Compare A (56.5 kPa, 34% O₂) with B (101.3 kPa, 21% O₂). Their oxygen partial pressures are 19.21 and 21.27 kPa. Try He or Ar, choose a material and set an oxygen range. Read the two endpoint runs, crew use and airlock losses. The flame temperature assumes idealized burning and can exceed the actual temperature. Check Lunar margins for the selected specimen’s reported conditions.

Design, run and export

Open the vehicle designer. Select parts, place the vehicle, set the gas and add an interior item. Compare a material swap, inspect what your sensors would measure, and export the assumptions. The evidence panel counts matching archived experiments. The physics validation page explains how the model was checked.

Measure a real flight sequence

Open Measure a flame video and expand Show worked measurement · luminous contour. The bright front in five Saffire-I images moves from x = 408 to 457 pixels in 14 seconds, or 3.50 px/s. The 30 mm calibration grid still needs to be aligned with the specimen plane to convert this to mm/s. Open an original frame or download the record to check the measurement.
